solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Gruesome camera shot features burglar's head

indicators.note: something that features an item has it within, so the burglar's letter sits inside the rearranged word
shot in the sense of ruined or worn out, so the letters of camera are knocked into a new order
the head of the word burglar's is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A grim photo shows a burglar's head caught on a security camera.
explanation.definitionFit: Macabre describes things that dwell on death and horror, a close synonym of gruesome.

clue.text: Separating from masked man?

parts.note: cryptically, someone masked could be a diver, who wears a face mask underwater
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A question about splitting off from a masked figure, perhaps a superhero.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'masked man' as a masked GENT, i.e. a DIVER GENT: the diver wears a mask under water.
explanation.definitionFit: Divergent paths are ones moving apart from each other, so the adjective matches separating.

clue.text: Having emptied supply, originate order

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving only the first and last letters of supply

parts.note: to stem from something is to originate there

explanation.surface: Instructions for clearing out supplies and starting a new arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is an orderly arrangement or method, so the noun order is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Posh — initially confused by intuitive style

indicators.note: the first letters of the two words are mixed up, each taking the other's opening letter

parts.note: a gut feeling is an intuitive one
class means style or elegance, as in a player with real class

explanation.surface: Someone posh is first bewildered by an instinctive way of doing things.
explanation.walkthrough: GUT and CLASS swap their initial letters, G and C, giving CUT GLASS.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-glass accent is a very refined, upper-class British way of speaking.

clue.text: Bog standard fare?

parts.note: bog is British slang for a toilet, also called a convenience, so standard toilet food is jokingly ready-made meals

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bog standard' means ordinary in British slang, but read 'bog' as a toilet, a public convenience; ordinary fare is ready-prepared food.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready meals and processed snacks needing little preparation are what this phrase names: unremarkable, everyday eating.

clue.text: Shed's worth?

parts.note: the letters of throw, set off (rearranged), spell worth; so the answer read as wordplay produces this word

explanation.surface: A question about what a garden shed might be worth.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: treat the answer itself as wordplay, THROW with OFF as a signal to rearrange it, and the result is worth.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed something, like a coat or a pursuer, is to cast it away or get rid of it.

clue.text: Northern city is pioneer in broadcasting

indicators.note: broadcasting means spoken over the air, so what is heard stands in for the written word

parts.note: someone who is a pioneer leads the way

explanation.surface: A northern city claims to have led the way in television and radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a large city in Yorkshire, in the north of England.

clue.text: Drag empty barrel — pity about that

indicators.note: the word for pity goes around, and so contains, the shortened barrel

parts.note: as in 'what a shame', a shame is a pity

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its inner letters, leaving the first and last of barrel

explanation.surface: Someone hauling an empty barrel along, and what a pity that is.
explanation.definitionFit: To shamble is to walk awkwardly, shuffling and dragging the feet.

clue.text: Neglect it after cross is in place

indicators.note: these letters sit inside the word for place

parts.note: to lay something is to place it down

indicators.note: the word it comes after the cross

parts.note: a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: An instruction to ignore something once a cross has been put in position.
explanation.definitionFit: Laxity is slackness or carelessness, a failure to take due care, which is what neglect means.

clue.text: New Avengers weapon

indicators.note: something new is in fresh form, so the letters of Avengers are rearranged

explanation.surface: A weapon from a new series of The Avengers, the British spy TV show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Avengers' looks like the title of the TV series The New Avengers, but 'New' signals rearranging the letters of Avengers.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve gas is a chemical warfare agent that attacks the nervous system.

clue.text: Puzzle — what fills K-W? Good luck!

parts.note: a maze is a puzzle of paths
the letters between K and W in the alphabet run from L to V, written as L TO V

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter asks what goes in a gap and wishes the solver well.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters that fill the stretch from K to W are L to V, giving L TO V.
explanation.definitionFit: Mazel tov is a Yiddish and Hebrew expression literally meaning good fortune, used as congratulations.

clue.text: Used to be — albeit oddly — pungent Japanese stuff

parts.note: was is the past tense of be

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth, of albeit

explanation.surface: Something that once was, odd though it seems, a sharp Japanese food.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasabi is the hot green horseradish-like paste served with sushi.

clue.text: Interpreter has to continue to entertain academic

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within, so the degree sits inside

parts.note: to drag on is to continue tediously
an MA, Master of Arts, is an academic

explanation.surface: A translator must keep entertaining a university lecturer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoman was an official translator and guide in Turkish, Arabic or Persian-speaking lands.

clue.text: Find out about exceptional light source

indicators.note: the rearranged word goes around the word for exceptional
out in the sense of wrong or disordered, so the letters of find are rearranged

parts.note: something rare is exceptional or uncommon

explanation.surface: Discover all about an unusual source of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Infrared is radiation just beyond red in the spectrum, giving off heat as invisible light.

clue.text: It turned to desert in some distant past

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the reversed word and desert go inside the word for some

parts.note: any means some, as in 'have you any money'

indicators.note: turned around means the word It is read backwards

parts.note: to quit a place is to desert it

explanation.surface: Something that turned into desert at some point long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'It' as land turning into desert, but here 'It' is just two letters to be reversed and 'desert' is the verb meaning to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiquity means ancient times, the far-off ages before the Middle Ages.

clue.text: Ball carried by trained bats, rats etc

indicators.note: the ball is carried inside the rearranged letters
bats means crazy, so the letters of trained go haywire

parts.note: a ball is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A ball is carried around by trained bats and rats in a circus act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' looks like describing the bats, but it is the fodder and 'bats' (crazy) signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodentia is the zoological order of gnawing mammals, including rats, mice and squirrels.

clue.text: Failure appeared to embody small part of football team

indicators.note: to embody is to contain within, so the abbreviation goes inside

parts.note: shown means appeared, as in 'he never shown up'; displayed
UTD is the short form of United, part of many British football team names such as Manchester Utd

explanation.surface: A failure seemed to be personified by a small part of a football side.
explanation.definitionFit: A shutdown is a stoppage or breakdown, as when a system fails and ceases operating.

clue.text: Try getting house across road with a grand

indicators.note: the abbreviation for house stretches across, around, the other letters

parts.note: AVE is the abbreviation for avenue, a road
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: An attempt at buying a house over the road for a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: Have a go is an informal idiom for attempt, as in 'let me have a go'.

clue.text: Bishop takes over violent town

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over
rough means violent, as in rough treatment

explanation.surface: A bishop takes control of a lawless town.
explanation.definitionFit: A borough is a town with its own corporation or a district of a large city.

clue.text: Hard to get prisoner outside a prison

indicators.note: the word for prisoner wraps around the outside of the rest

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: It is hard for a convict to get out of a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast-iron means rigid and unbreakable, as in a cast-iron guarantee, so it is firm and tough.

clue.text: Strokes cap one has thus placed on head

indicators.note: in a down entry the word for thus is put on top, at the head of the rest

parts.note: so means thus, as in 'and so it was'
a lid is a cap or cover
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A hat placed on someone's head with careful strokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A solidus is the slanting stroke, or slash, used in writing fractions; solidi is its plural.

clue.text: Ornate steel rims very elegant

indicators.note: to rim something is to surround it, so the rearranged letters enclose the abbreviation
ornate suggests elaborately reworked, so the letters of steel are rearranged

explanation.surface: Decorative steel wheel rims are very stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Svelte means slender and graceful in figure, so it is a synonym for elegant.

clue.text: Forest dweller catches bird in both hands

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it inside

parts.note: L and R, the abbreviations for left and right, the two hands
an emu is a large flightless bird

explanation.surface: A woodland creature grabs a bird with its two hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemurs are primates native to Madagascar that mostly live in trees in its forests.

clue.text: Attack lover, describing love jerk rejected

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw around, so the lover's word goes around the rest

parts.note: a fan is a lover or devotee of something

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so love and jerk together are read backwards

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
to jerk is to pull sharply

explanation.surface: A spurned lover turns on a jerk who rejected them.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall upon someone is to assault them suddenly, an idiom for attack.

clue.text: Plant pot with metal flaps

indicators.note: to be in a flap is to be agitated, so the letters of pot and metal are thrown about

explanation.surface: A plant pot fitted with metal flaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A palmetto is a small fan palm, a plant of the south-eastern United States.

clue.text: Rabbit seizing dog's weakness

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so the word for dog sits inside

parts.note: a doe is a female rabbit
to dog someone is to follow them, to tag along after

explanation.surface: A rabbit catching hold of a dog shows its frailty.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotage is the feeble condition of old age, a mental weakness or senility.

clue.text: Low, extremely rural and open countryside

parts.note: to low is to moo like cattle

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, taken from rural

explanation.surface: Low-lying, very rural, wide-open land.
explanation.definitionFit: Moorland is open, uncultivated upland covered in heather and grass.
